rule: In every fold the held-out cohort(s) contribute NO node, NO signature and NO vote on the cut: the fold's signature table holds training-cohort rows only (asserted row by row), and clustering, cut choice, refinement, nesting, naming, prototypes and the unreliable flags are all computed from that table alone.
note: benchmark_protocol.yaml label_space.primary_rule and leakage_rules.test_cohort_label_space_construction = forbidden. Folds: the 7 LOCO folds plus the 2 LOTO folds that differ from a LOCO fold (breast = Keren + Danenberg, skin = Phillips + ferguson). The other 3 LOTO folds hold out one cohort and ARE their LOCO fold (protocol splits.secondary).

rule: SIM and EV between training labels, computed from the fold's own table, are bit-identical to the same block of the full 7-cohort build
note: Carried from gate1b_control_expect.csv check 1. rescale() and containment() work one cohort at a time, so dropping a cohort should move nothing else. If it holds, the held-out-to-training distances used for placement (row 3) come from the same geometry the partition was cut in. If it fails, STOP: placement would compare held-out labels against a moved target.

rule: The fold runs the SHIPPED Stage 1b chain unchanged (s1b_control.run: rescale -> containment -> choose_cut -> cluster -> refine -> nesting -> name_clusters) with the shipped v4 switches (weighted RMS, label QC, midrange centring, straddle guard) and the shipped cut rule: the most LOCO-stable cut inside the usable window. No --seed-refine, no per-fold tuning.
note: The fold's OWN cut ships, not the shipped 0.800: 0.800 was chosen with the held-out cohort present, so reusing it would carry the held-out cohort's vote on granularity into the fold. A fold with NO usable cut falls back to the whole sweep exactly as Stage 1b does, and is marked no_usable_cut in every downstream table - never silently.

rule: Each held-out native label (after label QC) joins the frozen cluster whose members are closest ON AVERAGE (distance from the full build), and is admitted only if that average is <= the fold's cut tau and below FAR. Otherwise it is NOVEL (cluster -1): never forced into the nearest cluster. NOVEL cells are dropped from the closed-set macro-F1 and counted for the open-set metrics.
note: The admission rule the partition was built with - average linkage, as if the label had arrived last. Same rule as s7_spaces.assign_frozen and s9_newcohort.place; factored into one function so the three cannot drift. benchmark_protocol.yaml label_space.test_label_mapping and unsupported_label_rule.

rule: Recomputed INSIDE the fold with the shipped Gate 1b rule: every case in gate1b_v4_expect.csv is scored on the fold partition using only its members from the fold's TRAINING cohorts; a same/different case left with < 2 members, or a nested case missing its child or parent, is n/a. A required case marked waived in v4 that FAILS in the fold flags the clusters of its remaining members, minus the shipped exemption (>= 3 tissues, positive-marker name, holds the case's plurality, not the largest cluster). Blob-proof scoring, fold-local. Held-out labels never flag a cluster.
note: LIMITATION, stated: WHICH cases are waived was decided after seeing the full 7-cohort build, so the waiver list is not blind to any held-out cohort. It is a declared scoring input (like the case list itself), and it only decides which classes the reliable-class headline leaves out - the all-class macro-F1 is reported beside it (protocol layer_2 macro_f1_all_classes_note).

rule: per fold: tau, clusters, usable window yes/no, cohort_ari, biggest cluster share, clusters flagged unreliable and their cell share
note: PREDICTION written before the run: at least one fold picks a cut other than 0.800. D-47 measured the stability curve flat to within 0.0035 on the old roster, so the cut choice is close to a coin flip among legal options.

rule: per fold: held-out labels and cells admitted vs NOVEL, and for each NOVEL label its nearest average distance against tau
note: PREDICTION written before the run: the NOVEL share is highest for Sorin (17-marker panel, fewest shared markers with most cohorts) and for ferguson (whose EC placement already rested on a 0.009 margin). A fold with zero NOVEL labels is not evidence of good placement on its own.

rule: ARI between the fold space and the shipped label_map.csv over (i) the fold's training labels and (ii) training + admitted held-out labels, cell-weighted and unweighted; plus the same at a MATCHED cut 0.800 as a diagnostic that is never shipped
note: The matched-cut row separates 'the held-out cohort changed the partition' from 'it changed the granularity', as B2 did for the H10 control (matched-cut ARI 0.9828 on the old roster). PREDICTION: matched-cut weighted ARI >= 0.85 in every fold; own-cut ARI lower wherever the cut moved.

rule: work/spaces/label_map_{fold}.csv (Stage 1b format; NOVEL rows kept with cluster -1), work/spaces/prototypes_{fold}.npy (the fold's own centroids - the held-out cohort contributes nothing), and reports/s1b_folds.md with the SHA-256 of each map
note: benchmark_protocol.yaml required_outputs.label_space. Stage 3 and Stage 6 read the fold's map and prototypes for that fold; the shipped work/label_map.csv stays the whole-roster space used for layer-1 reporting and is described as NOT blind to any held-out cohort.
